_description: Disagreements recorded by the classical sources *inside* a counting system, between the authorities through whom the system was transmitted. The vendored qiraat-ayah-map primitives give each system one settled position per point; this overlay says where the system's own authorities differ, so an edition's choice at such a point can be named rather than reported as an error. Anchors use the same (surah, kufi ayah, kind, word) key as the primitives. Every entry cites its source. An entry whose source attests the khilāf without naming who holds each side carries an empty `authorities` map; the edition files then say `authorities_named: false` rather than emitting sides the source does not give. When qiraat-ayah-map models this itself (their issue #11), entries here are deleted in favour of theirs.

source.work: الفرائد الحسان في عدّ آي القرآن
source.author: عبد الفتاح القاضي
source.note: قَرِيبًا الْبَصْرِى وَخُلْفٌ مَكِّهِمْ — «عده البصري والمكي يخلف عنه وتركه الباقون»
source.why: al-Dānī's al-Bayān gives the point to Baṣrī alone («عدها البصري ولم يعدها الباقون», sūrah 78, 41 āyahs in Baṣrī and 40 in the rest). al-Farāʾid al-Ḥisān records khilāf within Makkī at the same word, which is what the KFGQPC Bazzī edition follows. The source does not name the authorities on either side.
